name: Gixo
summary: Seven separate AI workspaces — decks, articles, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal drafts and books — each sold on its own plan.
best_for: teams that want one dedicated, source-grounded tool per deliverable — a deck tool, a content tool, a proposal tool — and would rather buy them separately than bend one generic generator into every shape
skip_if: you want a single flat AI subscription covering writing and design together, or you cannot justify stacking three narrow products to cover what one all-in-one tool does under one price
honest_knock:
Two things about this pricing are worth reading twice.

The first is that seven products means seven subscriptions. Gixo is priced per deliverable, not per company, and one product's plan does not include the others. A team that needs decks, articles and proposals buys Lumen plus Quill plus Arc: $69 a month at the one-seat entry tiers, and $253 a month at the tiers Gixo itself recommends for each (Lumen Professional $45, Quill Professional $79, Arc Professional $129). There is no published bundle price; the only route the page names is procurement, where private offers and multi-product bundles go through review. Ask for that before you subscribe to the second product, not after.

The second is the shape of the ladders, now that they are public (read 4 October 2026). The steps buy seats, review and brand control; the generation allowance behind each tier is still not stated outside Folio's chapter counts. And the first step is steep on Quill: Lite at $10 is pitched at publishing now and then, the next tier is $59. Run the 14-day trial at the volume you actually expect, because that volume decides which of those two prices you pay.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-04 on gixo.ai/pricing; the per-product floors are unchanged since 19 August 2026, but the page now publishes every tier) Gixo is not one product but seven, each bought on its own plan, priced in USD per month with an annual figure per tier. Quill: Lite $10 (1 seat, $90 a year), Starter $59 (1 seat, $599), Professional $79 (3 seats, $799), Business $99 (5 seats, $999), Enterprise $129 (10 seats, $1,299). Lumen: Lite $10 ($90), Starter $25 ($250), Professional $45 (2 seats, $450), Business $55 (5, $550), Enterprise $99 (10, $999). Prism: Starter $10 ($90), Professional $25 (2 seats, $250), Business $45 (5, $450), Enterprise $99 (10, $999). Business: Starter $19 ($190), Professional $49 (3 seats, $499), Business $59 (5, $599), Enterprise $79 (10, $799). Folio: Author $19 for 10 AI-drafted chapters a month and Pro $99 for 50, one seat each, with no annual figure. Lex: Solo Pilot $29 ($261), Solo $99 ($999), Small Firm $149 (3 seats, $1,499), Growing Firm $179 (5, $1,799), Marketplace $229 (10, $2,299). Arc: Starter $49 ($490), Professional $129 (2 seats, $1,299), Business $149 (5, $1,499), Enterprise $179 (10, $1,799). Generation allowances are not quantified on the page except Folio's chapters. The FAQ still says a no-card 14-day trial with full generation, that continued generation after it needs a paid plan while existing work stays viewable, and that there is no standing unpaid tier. Folio is described three ways: “Monthly book plans” on its card, “14-day trial, no card” in the comparison table, and starting free for planning and import in the introduction. Quill, Lumen, Business, Arc and Lex can also be bought through Microsoft Azure Marketplace, where private offers and multi-product bundles are handled through procurement review.

compare_with.name: Gamma or Beautiful.ai
compare_with.why: Gamma and Beautiful.ai do one job — turn a prompt into a presentable deck — and publish a single per-seat price you can multiply in your head. Gixo spreads the same AI drafting across seven separately priced products covering decks, content, visuals, briefs, proposals, legal work and books, so it reaches further and costs more to assemble. If decks are the whole job, the single-purpose tools are simpler and cheaper; if you want the same draft-review-export flow across several deliverables, that breadth is the thing Gixo actually sells. Verify all current price lists yourself; ours were read on 4 October 2026.
